cohort: The study included 20484 women without previous history of chronic kidney disease (CKD) who had deliveries over 10 years at a single center.
finding: The incidence of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) is increasing, and among patients with nephrological follow-up, decreased eGFR, evidence of CKD, or residual hypertension are common, with metabolic conditions (obesity, diabetes mellitus) identifying those at higher risk of actionable short-term adverse kidney outcomes.
followup_time: Up to 12 months for assessment of decreased eGFR, with general follow-up after discharge for other outcomes.
